findings.title: North Korea Steals USD 6.36 Billion From Binance in the Largest Hack in History
findings.summary_md: TRM Labs attributes the October 29, 2026 Binance theft of approximately USD 6.36 billion to North Korea's TraderTraitor unit. The attacker moved funds across ten blockchains in about 20 minutes starting at 20:05 UTC, using an EIP-7702 delegation to compromise a Binance hot wallet. About USD 2.7 billion was frozen by stablecoin issuers and the Arbitrum Security Council, leaving roughly USD 2.4 billion still under attacker control.

findings.title: 29 October Binance Security Incident: Initial Findings and Response Update
findings.summary_md: Binance published its initial findings on the October 29 security incident, confirming that at 00:10 UTC on October 30, 2026, a new authorization from the Binance14 hot wallet cleared the EIP-7702 delegation code. The post serves as the vendor's own advisory on the compromise, noting the investigation is ongoing.

findings.title: North Korea is likely culprit behind $6.3bn crypto hack, 'largest heist in history'
findings.summary_md: The Guardian reports that North Korea is the likely culprit behind the $6.3 billion Binance crypto hack, calling it potentially the largest heist in history. The article covers the FBI attribution to the DPRK and the suspension of withdrawals across multiple networks following the October 29 theft.
